summary: Module 04 edited into one module. node tools/check.mjs --module 4 --lang en --words reports 0 errors and 3 warnings: figures not drawn yet, and the two unbuilt widgets (gradient-flow-explorer, ssm-kernel-explorer). The five session-ref warnings (#paper1-3, #what_goes_wrong, #review) are fixed in the plan JSON. The concept prose is 16,702 words against a plan target of 15,450, inside BRIEF's 13,000-17,000 band: s1 1052, s2 1107, s3 1364, s4 1385, s5 1593, s6 1130, s7 1152, s8 1636, s9 1127, s10 1400, s11 1190, s12 849, s13 1717. Of the 21 figures, 16 are kept: fig-04-1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17, 19, 20 and 21, and the text now refers to every one. Labs 3 and 4 were re-run with labrun --update after small code changes; only timing lines changed. Every lab number quoted outside the labs now matches the executed outputs. The plan JSON is still valid, and only its display fields and activity refs were changed.
changes: Fixed a mangled \rVert in Lab 1's Try-this item 4: the backslash-r had become a line break, so the line read 'Vert$'. Normalised 20-labs-a.md and 30-exercises.md from CRLF to LF like the other parts. The KaTeX errors the writers reported were already gone.

Reconciled the concept text with the executed labs. Section 4: Lab 1's closing-tag rate is now about one in five (21% in Lab 1, 14-25% for Lab 2's RNN). Section 5 'What the labs show': plain RNN 14-25%, LSTMs 74-86% over two seeds, and which LSTM leads depends on the seed; bias 3 or 5 keeps the gradient ratio at 0.14-0.4 to lag 100 (the old text had 16%, 75-79% and 93-99%, and a ratio near 0.2). Section 9's Lab 3 monitor: sigma 0.131, residual RMS 0.135 to about 0.21, excitation detected after 85 samples, stuck sensor after 19, 239 normal samples with no false alarms; '(expected values)' removed. Section 10: exposure bias 73/51% at length 12, 91/78% at length 8, and no gap at length 4; beam search 0/200 strings, token accuracy 51.8 to 52.5%; bottleneck 99/36/1%. Section 11: alignment peaks 0.65-0.83, and 99/36/1% without attention. Section 13: real Lab 5 CPU timings (1.4/0.5, 5.4/2.5, 25.7/18.9 ms), the FFT advantage stated as modest; loop and FFT agree to a few parts in 1e6 to 1e5; recall results from three seeds (the vanilla RNN learns lag 25 only partly, the bias-1 LSTM stays at chance, the bias-5 LSTM learns lag 100 on one seed of three).

Section 8: the 1.075/0.155 worked example is now attributed to a run made when the module was prepared. Its closing sentence now says that Lab 3 runs the same model on the drifting Duffing signal, where it also loses to naive (0.42 against 0.37, mean error -0.32), and that the fix gives 0.135. The removed Figure 4.13 is replaced by a pointer to Lab 3 Step 5 with the real horizon errors. Section 7's sonnet early-stopping figure is attributed to a preparation run, and Lab 1's Try-this item 3 now gives the sonnet numbers from the writer notes (2.46 against a bigram's 2.45 and a trigram's 2.26).

What goes wrong: the LSTM-vs-persistence entry adds Lab 3's 0.42/0.37 and drops 'published code'. The closing-tag entry now says 'one line in five against one in eight'. The padding entry cites Lab 4 Step 7 (100% padded, 0% cut to width). Exposure bias is 73/51%. The multi-step entry now reads 0.73 against naive's 0.78. Exercise 9's prompt and solution use 73/51% (now 1.8 times as many errors) and the per-length numbers. Exercise 8(d) quotes Lab 3's 5 offset alarms and labels its own numbers as the Exercise 15 re-implementation. The summary bullet on Lab 4 now reads 99% to 1%.

Removed source references from Lab 3. Step 2 is retitled 'Section 8's mistake, run as written'. The code comment is now 'Step 2', the variable source_model is global_model, and the plot label is 'LSTM, global z-score'. The prose says 'Section 8's code' or 'the globally normalised model'. 'Parts C and D' became 'Steps 5 and 6'. Lab 2's 'planning machine' run-time line now gives the measured about 10 s per model. Lab 3 was re-run with labrun --update; only timings changed.

One symbol per quantity. Section 11's attention parameters were W_s, W_h and v, and W_h clashed with the recurrent matrix W_h. They are now Bahdanau's W_a, U_a and v_a throughout Section 11, Lab 4 (prose and code attributes; Lab 4 re-run, outputs identical except timings), Exercise 11 (prompt, solution and code) and quiz question 9, and Section 11 says once why. Lab 1 Step 4 used delta for dL/dz and g for the logit gradient, the reverse of Section 3; it now follows Section 3 (delta = dL/dh, g = dL/dz, dL/dy at the logits, mapped to the code names dh, dz, g) and writes the target character as c_{t+1}, not y_t, which clashed with the bold logits. Lab 2 Step 1 called the pre-activation chunks i, f, g, o, which clashed with the gate values f_t. They are now z_i, z_f, z_g, z_o, mapped to Section 5's gates.

Figures: 5 removed, leaving 16. fig-04-2 repeated the parameter worked example. fig-04-5 repeated the w^n table, which the widget also shows. fig-04-8 repeated the forget-bias table. fig-04-13 repeated Lab 3 Step 5's plot and carried plan values. fig-04-18 repeated Lab 4 Step 6's heat-map and bars; the text now points to Lab 4 Step 6. Two captions changed. fig-04-14's bottom half is now schematic fault signatures, not '(expected values)' lab panels. fig-04-19 no longer repeats the comparison table. fig-04-4's caption now has left and right panels. The text now refers to Figures 4.4, 4.11, 4.14, 4.15, 4.16, 4.20 and 4.21.

Continuity: Section 1's preview table now fills in the attention row's sequential steps (1 per layer, Section 12). Section 12 now links '[Exercise 15](#e15)'. Fixed Lab 5's typo 'in over repeated runs' and its speed-up range, which now reads 2.5-5x to match the run shown. Removed an empty output fence after Lab 5's plot block.

References: added Cho, van Merrienboer, Bahdanau and Bengio 2014 (SSST-8), cited in Section 10; Williams and Peng 1990 (Section 3); Hochreiter's 1991 diploma thesis (Section 4); and Karpathy's 2015 essay (Section 2). A script check found no other cited author-year pair missing from the list.

Plan JSON (plan/module_04.json), display fields only. The lead is now one sentence without 'This module'. Prerequisites and software are one sentence each; e^{i theta} became $e^{i\theta}$. The outcomes add maths in $...$: the half-life $\ln 0.5/\ln\sigma(b_f)$, the kernel $\mathbf{C}\mathbf{A}^k\mathbf{B}$ and $\Delta_t$. Session titles became 'Gates and memory' and 'What came back, and review'. Every activity 'what' is one sentence that names Sections and Exercises in full. Refs paper1/2/3 now point to reading, what_goes_wrong to wrong and review to summary; the review activity refs wrong, summary and terms. Minutes are unchanged (620 in total). A backup is in the scratchpad at m04bak/.
issues: The plan's sections[].figures, writer_notes and widget defaults still list the 5 removed figures (fig-04-2, 5, 8, 13, 18) and the plan-era lab numbers, because only display fields were in scope. The figure phase should draw only the 16 ids that remain in the text.

Some numbers come from runs made when the module was prepared, not from executed lab code, and are labelled that way in the text. They are Section 8's 1.075/0.155 and 'about 0.12 to 0.14' (sinusoid with drift), Section 7 and Lab 1 Try-this item 3's sonnet results (about 250 updates; 2.46 against 2.45/2.26), Lab 2's second seed (79%/74%), Lab 3's second seed, and Lab 5's seeds 1 and 2. None was re-verified here.

Section 4's simulation numbers come from NumPy default_rng(1). The widget uses mulberry32, so its default curve will differ by a factor of a few; the text says that other draws change the numbers by a factor of a few.
s9 (+19%), s13 (+18%) and s7 (+15%) are the sections furthest over their targets. The no-shortening rule kept them, and the module total is still inside BRIEF's band.

labrun reports 'SOME LABS NEED ATTENTION' for Labs 3 and 4 only because timing lines differ between runs; every computed value matched. Labs 1, 2 and 5 were not re-run, because their code was not changed.

Several prose lines in the parts are longer than 100 characters, mostly where the writers joined inline maths onto one line to avoid KaTeX list-marker failures. They render correctly and were not reflowed.
The guided-reading descriptions of Pascanu 2013, Bahdanau 2015 and Mamba refer to the papers by topic and were not re-checked online.
